chunks: In the narration of al-Sakūnī, it is reported that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:
For the private part of the male child, there is diyyah, and for the private part of the impotent man, there is diyyah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: prescribed blood money or financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.ذَكَرِ الصَّبِيِّ: the male organ of a boy
key_terms.ذَكَرِ الْعِنِّينِ: the male organ of an impotent man

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyyah for injury to the private part of a boy or an impotent man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on bodily injury compensation. It states that injury to the male organ of a boy and of an impotent man entails full blood money (diyyah), indicating that such compensation is not negated by young age or impotence.
